title: Montclair Diagnostics — Governance, Sizing, and KPI Scoping
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week pilot focused on access controls, compliance gates (SOC2/ISO), SSO + SCIM, RBAC at model & route level, audit log retention, and throughput/latency benchmarks. Agreed high-level success criteria, initial workload sizing, and a bench plan for p50/p95 latencies and qps targets. Action: Redwood to produce security whitepaper, sample SOC2 evidence checklist, and a benchmark runbook; Montclair to provide 48-hour sample dataset and traffic profile.
topics: Workload sizing: qps, batch sizes, concurrency
Benchmarks: p50/p95 latency targets and throughput
Fallbacks: hosted vs dedicated vs private

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-04 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (CSM), Dr. Elena Morris (CTO, Montclair), Marcus Li (Infra Lead), Tanya Blake (Head of Security), Omar Reyes (ML Eng)

Summary / Opening (00:00):
[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i know we're spread across timezones so we'll try to be crisp. this is the scoping call for the montclair diagnostics pilot, the focus as we agreed is governance and performance acceptance. ravi will cover the bench plan and i'll walk through compliance asks.
[00:18] Dr. Elena: thanks jamie. quick background — we're building triage assistant for lab technicians and clinicians, data is sensitive (PHI adjacent), must stay in eu for production ideally. we want a pilot to prove performance, security and operational controls before we escalate to a year contract.
[00:34] Tanya: hi, from security my top concerns are: SOC 2 evidence, iso27001 alignment, SSO (Okta) and scim provisioning, tight rbac by team and model, and immutable audit logs with 7 year retention for certain events.

Discovery / Requirements (00:45 - 12:00):
[00:45] Jamie: notes — regional residency: eu-germany preferred, okta + scim, separate dev/prod spaces, audit logs retention var for different events. any red lines?
[01:10] Tanya: we need HSM-backed key management for prod keys, ideally customer-managed KMS, and ability to rotate keys without downtime. also need to see sample audit records for admin actions and model inferences.
[01:32] Ravi: quick Q — for benching, do you expect encrypted kv cache or is plaintext okay in pilot? this affects perf.
[01:40] Marcus: for pilot we can do encrypted but realistic tests should mimic prod — so KV in encrypted mode, yes.
[02:03] Omar: our peak is around 300 qps for text classification routes with median payload ~600 tokens, 95th around 1200 tokens. we batch on client side currently 4–8.
[02:28] Ravi: thanks — that's helpful. we'll plan for both per-route microbenchmarks and a blended test with 300 qps +/- 30%.

Success criteria & KPIs (12:00 - 22:00):
[12:01] Jamie: proposed success criteria (open for edits):
- functional: SSO + SCIM provisioning works for 3 test users, RBAC enforces route-level access (dev vs prod).
- security: SOC2 checklist items mapped, sample evidence delivered.
- performance: p50 latency < 120ms for classification route (600 tokens), p95 < 420ms; throughput sustain 300 qps with p95 < 800ms under steady state; cold start behavior documented.
- reliability: no more than 0.1% error rate for the 6-hour sustained run.
[12:40] Dr. Elena: those targets look reasonable but p50 120ms might be tight given our token sizes and encryption. can we set an alternate for hosted vs dedicated?
[12:52] Ravi: absolutely — we can show a matrix: hosted API (lowest friction) p50 160ms / p95 500ms; dedicated (reserved GPU) p50 110ms / p95 380ms; private on-prem numbers TBD. we'll include quantized model variants in the matrix.
[13:13] Marcus: cost targets are also important — we need per-inference cost to be under $0.003 for the classification flow otherwise product economics don't work.
[13:22] Jamie: we'll run cost estimates as part of the runbook, include token counts and batching to show unit economics.

Security / Compliance Deep-dive (22:00 - 37:00):
[22:01] Tanya: can you explain your RBAC model? we need least-privilege and ability to restrict which teams can call which model versions. also admin audit logs must show who rolled a model and which keys were used.
[22:28] Ravi: in Redwood you can create roles scoped to org/project/model/route — you can bind groups (SCIM groups from Okta) to roles. Admin actions are logged with user, action, resource, timestamp. We also stream audit logs to customer SIEMs or S3 — retention config is per-customer.
[22:55] Tanya: what's in the audit record for inference events? do you log prompt text?
[23:05] Ravi: we log metadata (request id, user id, model id, token counts, latency, result hash) but not full prompt by default for privacy. You can opt-in to store prompts if needed, but that has compliance implications.
[23:26] Omar: important: for PHI-like data we cannot keep plaintext prompts. can we redact on ingest?
[23:33] Ravi: yes we support redaction hooks and prefix/hash-only storage. we can also run a redaction lambda before persisting prompt bodies.
[24:10] Tanya: HSM/KMS specifics?
[24:16] Jamie: for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS + CloudHSM options). for hosted we offer encryption at rest with our keys, but enterprise customers can bring keys via KMS integration. rotation is available without downtime for active keys via key versioning.
[24:40] Tanya: need to see a runbook for key rotation and audit evidence.

Benchmark Plan / Workload Sizing (37:00 - 48:30):
[37:01] Ravi: bench plan outline:
- microbench per model variant (fp16 / int8 quant) with fixed payloads (600 tokens / 1200 tokens)
- concurrency sweep (1..32) to map latency vs qps
- sustained run: 6-hour job at 300 qps blended traffic with 10% spike windows at 450 qps
- cold-start spike tests and failover (simulate AZ loss)
We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, GPU utilization, memory, and token/sec.
[37:35] Marcus: for the sustained run we need to know batch sizing. any automatic batching?
[37:41] Ravi: Redwood runtime supports continuous batching; we'll test with batch sizes forced at 1, 4, 8 and runtime-optimized batching to measure cost/latency trade-offs.
[38:05] Omar: we prefer to test with KV-cache enabled since production will use it — affects latency significantly.
[38:12] Ravi: noted, we'll enable KV-cache for the primary runs and run a second set with empty cache to measure cold behavior.
[38:30] Jamie: target deliverables from bench: spreadsheet with raw metrics, latency curves, cost per 1M tokens, machine configs used (GPU type, memory, quant flags), and recommended deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) for expected SLAs.

Timeline & Milestones (48:30 - 54:30):
[48:31] Jamie: proposed 6-week pilot cadence:
- Week 0 (this week): sign-off on SOW and data access; send security docs (redwood)
- Week 1: environment setup, Okta SCIM test provisioning, baseline microbench runs
- Week 2: sustained benchmark and failover tests
- Week 3: security evidence collection and audit log shipping verification
- Week 4: business review — cost analysis and recommended config
- Week 5: run additional optimizations (quantized model, batch tuning)
- Week 6: final results, acceptance sign-off and next contract discussions
[49:20] Dr. Elena: that timeline seems tight but ok if we keep weekly check-ins.
[49:30] Lena: CSM will set recurring weekly 30-min syncs; i'll send invites.

Objections / Tradeoffs discussed (54:30 - 55:00):
[54:30] Marcus: concern about on-prem private deployment effort — how long do you estimate for private install?
[54:38] Ravi: for full on-prem stack with HSM integration, we estimate 8–12 weeks, depends on network/VPN work. for the pilot we'll run in eu region dedicated capacity or private VPC with customer peering which is faster.
[54:55] Jamie: recap and next steps — we'll send the security whitepaper, SOC2 mapping, and bench runbook by friday, montclair to send sample traffic. we locked owners on the action items. thanks all.
